Comment: ABS (intransitive S and transitive O) is zero-marked; no dedicated ABS suffix (§2.3, p.344).
1st person pronouns have the same form for subject and object functions (§3.1.4, p.349). Grammatical role of 1st/2nd person encoded through verb prefixes (N-), not through nominal ERG suffix.
2nd person pronouns also have invariant form; role encoded through verb prefixes.
No dedicated 3rd person pronouns; demonstratives serve as 3rd person (§3.1, §3.4) and DO take ERG suffix -'is: je'is (dem-ERG). Confirmed at §3.3 and §2.3.
Full NPs take ERG suffix -'is when transitive subjects (§2.3: 'El viento derribó a un árbol grande' with sava'is = wind-ERG).
Continuative/imperfective aspect (-pa) co-occurs with ERG marking: yomo'is tyonvitu'yajpa 'The women turn the tortillas' (§2.1.2). No aspect-based split.
Preterite/completive (-u) also co-occurs with ERG marking (§2.3). No aspect-based split.
Preterite examples consistently show ERG -'is on transitive subjects.
Present/continuative and future contexts also show ERG -'is. No tense-based split.
All indicative constructions show ERG marking on 3rd person and full NP transitive subjects.
ERG -'is applies in subordinate and modal contexts (§11.3, §15.2); participial relative clauses explicitly require -'is on transitive subjects (§15.2.1).
All realis (indicative) contexts show ERG marking.
Future (manba), conditional (oca si), and purpose clauses (va'co) also show ERG -'is on transitive subjects.
ERG marks 'the person responsible for the effect of the action of the transitive verb' (§2.3, p. 344; our translation of the Spanish original).
Causative prefix yac- creates transitive constructions with non-volitional/inanimate causers taking ERG -'is (sava'is = wind-ERG, p.344). ERG applies to non-agentive A.
No topicality conditioning described or implied; ERG -'is is a structural case suffix.
No topicality conditioning; ERG applies equally to non-topical A.
Animate A consistently takes ERG -'is (all canonical transitive subjects are animate).
Inanimate causers (e.g., wind-ERG, p.344) also take ERG -'is in causative constructions (§9.2.6).
All primary transitive main clause constructions show ERG marking.

Participial/relative clauses explicitly documented: 'If the relativised element is the subject of the transitive verb... the ergative suffix -'is is attached to the verb' (§15.2.1, p. 401; our translation of the Spanish original).
No additional conditioning beyond the person-based split (1st/2nd: verb agreement only; 3rd/NP: nominal suffix -'is). This split is already captured in GB409_2-3.
The ERG suffix -'is also marks possessors (§2.2.1, p. 342: 'The possessor noun takes the ergative suffix'; our translation of the Spanish original). Explicit ERG=GEN syncretism.
Instrumental/comitative expressed through postpositions (-pit 'with', -ji'n 'with', §5, pp.356-357), entirely distinct from ERG suffix -'is.
